name: Chase Ultimate Rewards
note: Best value transferring to airline/hotel partners or booking travel through the Chase portal (Sapphire Reserve/Preferred or Ink Business Preferred cardholders get the boosted portal rate).

redemption_methods.note: Hyatt is the reliable outlier — category 1-4 award nights routinely beat their own cash rate by roughly double.
United, Aeroplan and Flying Blue shine on long-haul and premium cabins; domestic economy often lands no better than the portal.

redemption_methods.method: Book travel through the Chase portal
redemption_methods.note: Sapphire Reserve and Preferred holders get the boosted rate, and there is no award availability to hunt for.
The flat floor. Fine if you genuinely need cash, but it hands back the entire transfer premium.

redemption_methods.method: Pay with points at Amazon or PayPal
redemption_methods.note: The easiest button in the portal and the worst rate in the program — barely half what a Hyatt transfer returns.

name: Amex Membership Rewards
note: Best value transferring to airline/hotel partners; Pay With Points and Amex Travel redemptions run well below that.

redemption_methods.note: Where nearly all Membership Rewards value lives — Flying Blue, Aeroplan and ANA premium-cabin awards are the sweet spots.
The one Amex Travel rate that is not bad, and it applies to flights only.
Marriott and especially Hilton dilute Membership Rewards badly. Price the cash rate before transferring.
Amex prices its cash-equivalent redemptions well below the industry norm.

redemption_methods.method: Pay With Points at checkout, or gift cards
redemption_methods.note: Amex's most visible redemption and its worst — under a third of what a transfer returns.

name: Southwest Rapid Rewards
note: No cash-out option; value here reflects typical redemption for Southwest flights. Used to discount points-denominated card credits (e.g. anniversary point bonuses) to real dollars.

redemption_methods.note: Southwest prices points against the cash fare, so the rate barely moves — the cheapest fares are where it lands best.
Same peg, higher fare bucket; you are buying flexibility rather than extra point value.

redemption_methods.method: Hotel and car bookings through Southwest
redemption_methods.note: Roughly half what a fare returns, for a booking you could make anywhere.

redemption_methods.method: Gift cards and merchandise in the Rapid Rewards store
redemption_methods.note: There is no cash-out door in this program, so the store is the bottom rung — about a third of what a fare gets you.

name: Wyndham Rewards
note: Fixed-category hotel award chart; conservative per-point estimate. Used to discount points-denominated card credits to real dollars.

redemption_methods.method: Free night at a top-tier property
redemption_methods.note: The flat 30,000-point tier is not capped by the cash rate, so expensive properties are where it pays.

redemption_methods.method: Free night at a standard property
redemption_methods.note: The 15,000-point tier — the everyday case, and what this program's default valuation reflects.
Priced per bedroom rather than per night; occasionally good, usually not.
Under half the value of even a standard free night.

name: United MileagePlus
note: Conservative per-mile estimate for United award redemptions. Used to discount points-denominated card credits to real dollars.

redemption_methods.method: Star Alliance partner awards in business class
redemption_methods.note: Partner premium cabins are the best use of MileagePlus by a wide margin.
Dynamic pricing moves this around, but saver-level economy is the dependable everyday case.

redemption_methods.method: Hotel and car awards through United
redemption_methods.note: A third less than a saver flight, for something no award chart protects.
United's non-travel redemptions are half the value of flying on the same miles.

name: JetBlue TrueBlue
note: Revenue-based program; per-point estimate for typical JetBlue redemptions. Used to discount points-denominated card credits to real dollars.

redemption_methods.method: Low-fare Blue and Blue Basic redemptions
redemption_methods.note: TrueBlue is revenue-based, so the rate is best on already-cheap fares.
The everyday case across most routes and fare buckets.
Points cover the flight portion at a worse rate than booking that flight on its own.
Less than half a flight redemption — the default bad door.

name: Bilt Rewards
note: Transfers 1:1 to an unusually strong partner list for a no-annual-fee card; the rent-credit and cash-equivalent doors are priced far below that, so the transfer premium is effectively the whole program.

redemption_methods.note: The same Hyatt sweet spot Chase points reach, at the same 1:1 ratio.
AAdvantage, Alaska and Aeroplan all transfer 1:1 — a strong list for a card with no annual fee.

redemption_methods.method: Book through the Bilt travel portal
redemption_methods.note: A fixed rate with no award availability to chase, but well under what transfers return.
The redemption the card is named for is not the one it rewards — it gives up a third of the value versus transferring.
Bilt prices its cash-equivalent door deliberately low — barely a quarter of a Hyatt transfer.
